_comment: Statutory aid-intensity ceilings per GBER article. This is REFERENCE DATA, not an inference: the numbers are set by Commission Regulation (EU) No 651/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/1315, and they are identical for every scheme granting under the article. That is what makes them safe to state where the scheme's own documents are silent — we are not guessing what this fund does, we are stating what the law caps it at. Each entry carries the paragraph it comes from. `verified` marks whether a human has checked the figure against the regulation text; unverified figures are still published as a CEILING (an upper bound is the safe direction to be wrong in) but never as an expected award. Cross-checked empirically on every load by ETL/terms/encode_article_intensity.py, which drops an article inference whose scheme has demonstrably paid ABOVE the ceiling.
_source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 651/2014 (GBER), consolidated to 2023-07-01 by Regulation (EU) 2023/1315.
_verified_against: Art. 25(5) and 25(6)(a)-(b) confirmed VERBATIM on 2026-08-01 against two independent reproductions of the article text: legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/651/article/25 (the retained-EU-law reproduction of the 2014 original) and forskningsradet.no/en/state-aid/articles-state-aid. Both give 100/50/25/50 for fundamental research / industrial research / experimental development / feasibility studies, +10pp medium and +20pp small, +15pp for effective collaboration or wide dissemination, and an 80% cap on industrial research and experimental development. EUR-Lex consolidated HTML and the OJ PDF both truncate or fail to render before Art. 25 on fetch, so those two stand in for the OJ itself.

StateAidObjectiveGberArt25.label: R&D project aid

uplifts.when: effective collaboration, or results widely disseminated

StateAidObjectiveGberArt25.note: The category is a property of the PROJECT, not the scheme, so the honest instrument-level statement is the band across categories the scheme plausibly funds.

excluded_from_band.fundamental_research: 100% is available only for fundamental research, which companies do not typically undertake; stating it as the top of a company-facing band is misleading.
excluded_from_band.feasibility_study: 50% applies to feasibility studies, a distinct award type rather than the project aid a founder is scoping.

uplifts_not_encoded._why: Real uplifts added to Art. 25(6) by Regulation (EU) 2021/1237, deliberately NOT encoded. Omitting an uplift understates the ceiling, and understating is the safe direction: a founder who plans against less public money over-raises privately, which is recoverable. Overstating sends them into a round short. They are recorded here so that a later reader knows they were considered and excluded, not missed.

multi_member_state_project.condition: selected by a Member State after an open call to form part of a project jointly designed by at least three Member States or EEA contracting parties

assisted_region_107_3_a.confidence: CONFLICTING — one source says 25pp, another says 15pp. Not encoded at any value until the Official Journal settles it. This is exactly the figure that must not be guessed: it is the largest of the three.

StateAidObjectiveGberArt25.cap_note: The 80% cap bounds every uplift, encoded or not, so a founder reading the encoded ceiling can never be told a number the article would not permit.

StateAidObjectiveGberArt25b.label: R&D project aid, feasibility-study variant
StateAidObjectiveGberArt25b.note: The Art. 25(6)(b) collaboration uplift is NOT recorded here: it is not confirmed to extend to feasibility studies, and inventing an uplift raises the stated ceiling, which is the unsafe direction.

StateAidObjectiveGberArt26.label: Investment aid for research infrastructures
StateAidObjectiveGberArt26.note: No SME uplift: the aid attaches to the infrastructure, not to an enterprise's size.

StateAidObjectiveGberArt28.label: Innovation aid for SMEs
StateAidObjectiveGberArt28.note: Art. 28(4) permits up to 100% for innovation advisory and support services where the total does not exceed EUR 200,000 per undertaking over any three years. Not encoded as a ceiling: it is conditional on a cumulation test we cannot evaluate per founder, and encoding it would raise the stated ceiling on every Art. 28 scheme.

StateAidObjectiveGberArt29.label: Aid for process and organisational innovation
StateAidObjectiveGberArt29.note: 15% for large undertakings, 50% for SMEs — a size split rather than an uplift, which is why it is two base categories.

StateAidObjectiveGberArt27.label: Aid for innovation clusters
StateAidObjectiveGberArt27.note: Assisted-area uplifts under Art. 27(7) are deliberately omitted: they depend on the cluster's NUTS location against the national regional aid map, which we hold for the instrument but not reliably for the cluster.

StateAidObjectiveGberArt21.label: Risk finance aid
StateAidObjectiveGberArt21.note: NO intensity ceiling exists, deliberately recorded rather than omitted. Risk finance is governed by private-participation rates and per-undertaking totals, not by a share of eligible costs. An encoder that treated a missing entry as 'unknown' would be free to invent one later; an explicit null says the concept does not apply.

StateAidObjectiveGberArt22.label: Start-up aid
StateAidObjectiveGberArt22.note: NO intensity ceiling. Art. 22 caps ABSOLUTE amounts (grants, loans, guarantees) by enterprise age and location, not a share of project cost. Recorded explicitly for the same reason as Art. 21.
StateAidObjectiveGberArt22.absolute_cap_note: Art. 22(3): grants capped at EUR 0.4M, rising to EUR 0.6M in Art. 107(3)(a) assisted areas and EUR 0.45M in Art. 107(3)(c) areas; small and innovative enterprises may receive double. The refutation test therefore uses the most PERMISSIVE reading (0.6M doubled = 1.2M) so that only a scheme paying far beyond any lawful Art. 22 grant is refuted.
StateAidObjectiveGberArt22.beneficiary_test: unlisted small enterprise under 5 years old

_corroboration: Realised aid INTENSITY cannot corroborate a SATR article: the transparency register publishes no project cost (0 of 122,814 SATR events), so a share of eligible costs is not computable there. It is available only on Horizon and Innovate UK, which do not carry inferred articles. The corroboration that IS available on SATR is the award AMOUNT against an article's absolute cap, and the recipient mix against an article's beneficiary restriction. Those are encoded below as `absolute_cap_eur` and `beneficiary_test`.
_band_policy: The published band is built from `company_categories`, NOT from every category the article covers. Art. 25 permits 100% for fundamental research, so the full span reads '25-100% of eligible costs' -- true, and useless: a company applying to a national R&D scheme is doing industrial research or experimental development, essentially never fundamental research, and a ceiling that opens at 100% invites a founder to plan against a number no company will see. Where the key is absent the band is the full span.
